title: Photosynthesis and respiration
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, sci-photosynthesis-respiration-carbon-cycle, is written for Year 9 and is broader than the brief, adding the carbon cycle, animals getting carbon from food, and steady atmospheric carbon dioxide, and its respiration card does not mention oxygen; changing that depth would be more than a small adaptation, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Photosynthesis and respiration
card: Plants use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. It happens in the green parts of a plant, in structures called chloroplasts.
Cells use glucose and oxygen to release energy. Carbon dioxide and water are also made.
Plants, animals and other living things all respire. Respiration happens all the time, in the light and the dark.
The two processes are linked. The products of one are the reactants of the other.
draft.remember: Photosynthesis stores energy in glucose. Respiration releases it.

a.q: Which pair of substances does a plant take in for photosynthesis?
a.why: Photosynthesis turns carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen, using light. Glucose and oxygen are what respiration uses, so they are not what photosynthesis takes in.
a.clue: Which two substances are on the starting side?

b.q: A potted fern sits in a dark cupboard overnight. What is happening in its cells?
opts: Both processes stop until light returns
Photosynthesis stops and the plant makes oxygen
b.why: Photosynthesis needs light, so it stops in the dark. Respiration happens all the time in living cells, so it carries on. Plants respire as well as photosynthesise, so it is wrong to say respiration stops.
b.clue: One process needs light and the other does not.
